name: Grebe
lede: Grebe is a dark, warm grey with a brownish cast, named for the plumage of the diving water bird.

sections.title: A bird's back
sections.body:
The color is listed in the 1930 Maerz and Paul dictionary, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system files its swatch under brownish gray [1]. None of the books read here describes it, so how the compilers chose the bird, and which grebe, is undocumented [1].

On screens the swatch is a muted grey-brown, close in family to [[taupe]], [[battleship-grey]] and [[pale-quaker-drab]] [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Grebe is not rare in painting: 740 of 23,781 museum paintings contain it, about 3.1 per cent, more than four-fifths of our named colors [2]. It most often plays a mid-tone, and it peaks in the 1900s, at 3.8 per cent of the paintings from those years [2]. The painter who leans on it most is [[painter:shen-zhou|Shen Zhou]], in 4 of his 12 works here, where it is likely the grey of ink and aged silk [2]. These are photographs of aged paintings, so the match is a look-alike hue, not a pigment test [2]. Its first match in the archive is a painting from 1119, 811 years before the name's earliest record in our sources [2].
